title: Soils
standard_code: Primary 2 Basic Science: Learning About Our Environment
standard_text: Soils differ in colour, texture and how much water they hold (sand, loam, clay); soil has living things; soil must be cared for. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 2, theme: Learning About Our Environment)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Learning About Our Environment): what is soil?, kinds of soil, living things in soil, caring for soil and soil investigations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Soil is a mixture of rock, humus, air and water.
key_sub: Sand drains fast, clay holds water, and loam is best for most plants.
body_html:
How to think about it

Soil is a mixture of tiny bits of rock, humus, air, water and living things.

  • Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water and is sticky; loam is a good mix.
  • Humus comes from decaying plants and animals and adds nutrients.
  • Worms, insects, fungi and bacteria live in soil and keep it healthy.
Example

Which soil drains fastest?

big spaces between grains

Answer: sandy soil

Example

How do worms help soil?

tunnels

mixing

Answer: they let in air and water

Common mistakes

  • Thinking soil is just dirt with nothing living in it.
  • Thinking all soils are the same.
  • Thinking worms harm gardens.

the middle layer, paler, with more stones and less humus

the middle layer, paler, with more stones and less humus
items.e: Topsoil on top, then subsoil, then bedrock.

items.q: Which of these is a natural part of soil: chocolate, paper clips, sand or sugar?

items.q: Which of these is a natural part of soil: chocolate, glass beads, paper clips or small stones?

items.q: Why is soil important to people?
c: We grow food in it and it filters water.
items.e: Healthy soil is a resource.

items.q: Which type of soil is a good mixture of sand, clay and humus that most plants like?
items.e: Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water; loam is a mixture most plants like.

items.q: Which kind of soil is best for growing most garden plants?
c: loam (a mix of sand, silt, clay and humus)
items.e: Loam holds water and drains well.

items.q: What is humus?
c: the dark part of soil made from decaying plants and animals
items.e: Humus gives soil nutrients.

items.q: Soil is shaken in a jar of water and left to settle for a day. Where will the bits of humus such as dead leaves end up?
c: near the top of the sediment
items.e: Heavy pieces sink first; light humus floats.

items.q: Soil is shaken in a jar of water and left to settle for a day. Where will the sand end up?
c: near the top of the sediment
items.e: Heavy pieces sink first; light humus floats.

items.q: What is composting?
c: turning food scraps and leaves into rich soil with the help of decomposers
items.e: Compost feeds plants.

items.q: Why is humus good for plants?
c: It adds nutrients and helps soil hold water.
items.e: Organic matter.

items.q: Where do earthworms like to live?
c: in dry sand in the sun
items.e: Living things help turn dead material into rich soil.

items.q: What is a decomposer?
c: an organism that breaks down dead plants and animals
items.e: Bacteria and fungi are decomposers. They feed on dead matter and wastes.

items.q: Why do gardeners add mulch around plants?
c: to keep soil moist and protect it from erosion
items.e: Mulch covers bare soil.

items.q: Which of these is a decomposer?
items.e: Mushrooms break down dead plants and animals. The others are producers or consumers.

items.q: How do earthworms help soil?
c: They take all the water out.
They mix it and make tunnels that let in air and water.
items.e: Living things help turn dead material into rich soil.

items.q: Why do earthworms help soil?
c: They mix it and make tunnels that let in air and water.
items.e: Healthy soil has many living things.

items.q: Why should people not drive off-road vehicles on wet trails?
c: They dig up soil and cause erosion.
items.e: Ruts channel water and wash soil away.

items.q: Which of these is a decomposer?
items.e: Fungi break down dead plants and animals. The others are producers or consumers.

items.q: Many Indigenous peoples see soil as part of Mother Earth. What does this teach?
c: to care for the land and give back to it
to use up the soil quickly
items.e: Respect for the land helps protect soil.

items.q: Zainab weighs the dead leaves in a compost bin every 2 weeks. How much mass did the leaves lose in 8 weeks?
items.e: 800 − 590 = 210 g. Decomposers broke down that much of the leaves.

items.q: Which soil lets water drain through fastest?
items.e: Sand has big grains with spaces between them.

items.q: What would happen if there were no decomposers?
c: Dead plants and animals would pile up, and soil would lose its nutrients.
items.e: Without decomposers, matter would stay locked in dead things instead of cycling back to plants.

items.q: Earthworms eat dead leaves and mix them into the soil. How do they help?
c: They help break down dead matter so nutrients return to the soil.
items.e: Earthworms and other small soil animals help decomposers by breaking dead matter into small pieces.

items.q: Why is bare soil easily eroded?
c: Nothing holds it in place against wind and rain.
items.e: Roots protect soil.

items.q: What happens to dead leaves on the ground over time?
c: They grow back on the tree.
They rot and become humus in the soil.
They stay the same for ever.
items.e: Living things help turn dead material into rich soil.

items.q: Nonso weighs the dead leaves in a compost bin every 2 weeks. Why does the mass go down?
c: Decomposers break the leaves down into nutrients, water and gases.
The leaves are destroyed and the matter is gone.
items.e: The matter is not destroyed. It goes into the soil as nutrients and into the air as carbon dioxide and water vapour.

items.q: Why are worms important to gardeners?
c: They help make soil healthy for plants.
items.e: Living things help turn dead material into rich soil.

items.q: What is the difference between a rock and a mineral?
c: Rocks are made of one or more minerals.
items.e: Granite is a rock made of quartz, feldspar and mica.

items.q: Which of these is a decomposer?
items.e: Bacteria break down dead plants and animals. The others are producers or consumers.

items.q: Which two kinds of organisms are the main decomposers?
items.e: Bacteria and fungi (like mould and mushrooms) do most of the decomposing.

items.q: Bisi's town needs to stop erosion this week. Choice 1: a row of trees (many years to grow). Choice 2: a sand fence (ready in 1 day). Which should they pick?
items.e: A sand fence can be ready this week.

items.q: Blessing's school has only a little money to stop soil washing away. Choice 1: a stone wall (costs a lot of money). Choice 2: grass (costs a little money). Which is the better choice?
items.e: Grass costs less.

items.q: What does a sand fence do on a beach?
c: It slows the wind so sand stays.
items.e: Slower wind drops sand.

items.q: Chidi reads: “A river floods and washes away its banks.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by water.

items.q: Hadiza's town needs to stop erosion this week. Choice 1: a sand fence (ready in 1 day). Choice 2: a row of trees (many years to grow). Which should they pick?

items.q: What happens to an apple core left in a compost bin for months?
c: It grows into a tree right away.
Decomposers break it down into soil.
items.e: Decomposition recycles nutrients.

items.q: How does soil help clean water?
c: Water is filtered as it soaks down through soil layers.
items.e: Soil acts like a filter.

items.q: The problem: Rain washes a dirt path into a ditch. Joy's plan: cover the path with wood chips. How does this help?
c: It makes the place look nice.
It helps because the straw protects the soil.
It helps because flat steps slow the water.
It helps because the chips slow the water.
items.e: Solutions slow wind or water.

items.q: Kemi sees a problem: Rain washes soil down a steep hill. What is a good solution?
items.e: Plant grass on the hill: the roots hold the soil.

items.q: How do plant roots help stop erosion?
c: They hold the soil in place.
items.e: Roots grip the soil.

items.q: Ife's town needs to stop erosion this week. Choice 1: a row of trees (many years to grow). Choice 2: sandbags (ready in 1 day). Which should they pick?
items.e: Sandbags can be ready this week.

items.q: What is a levee?
c: a high bank that keeps a river from flooding
items.e: It holds water in.

items.q: Nonso sees a problem: Rain washes soil off a garden bed. What is a good solution?

items.e: Cover the soil with straw: the straw protects the soil.

items.q: Which kind of soil drains water fastest?

items.q: Gbenga reads: “Water runs fast down a steep garden.” What is changing the land here?

items.q: Hauwa reads: “Rain washes soil off a garden bed.” What is changing the land here?

items.q: Which land will erode the most in heavy rain?

items.q: Tolu sees a problem: Wind blows soil off a big farm field. What is a good solution?

items.e: Plant a row of trees beside the field: the trees slow the wind.

items.q: Ada poured the same water on 4 model sand hills. Which cover kept the most sand in place?
items.e: The shortest bar lost the least sand: grass.

items.q: Which model best shows how matter moves in an ecosystem?

a cycle with arrows from air and soil to plants, plants to animals, and both to decomposers and back
items.e: Matter goes around in a cycle and is reused.

items.q: Abdullahi drops a little vinegar on four rocks. Only one fizzes. Which rock is it most likely to be?
items.e: Limestone contains calcium carbonate, which reacts with vinegar.
